evidence: Plin. NH 15.82: fīcīs mollis omnibus tāctus
terms.comment: Soft to touch, to sit or lie on, to eat; the opposite is dūrus (see hard). A soft voice is summissa vōx (see in a low voice).

terms.gloss: tender, soft (of young things and of food)
evidence: Sen. Ep. 123.2: tenerum et silīgineum, of bread

phrases.latin: fīcīs mollis omnibus tāctus, mātūrīs frūmenta intus
phrases.english: all figs are soft to the touch; ripe ones have seeds inside

phrases.latin: alicam in aquam īnfunditō. ubi bene mollis erit, in mortārium pūrum inditō
phrases.english: Put the groats in water. When they are nice and soft, put them in a clean mortar.

sources: Lewis & Short: mollis · Lewis & Short: tener
